options: A compression technique for large images
A recognisable image or pattern embedded into a digital or physical document to identify its authenticity or protect it from unauthorised use
A database index used to speed up searches
A timestamp recorded when a file is saved
A digital signature stored in file metadata
questions.explanation: A watermark is a recognisable image or pattern embedded into a document to identify its authenticity or protect it from unauthorised use.

questions.stem: In digital media such as images or videos, what form does a watermark often take?
options: A semi-transparent logo or text overlaid onto the content
A checksum appended to the file
questions.explanation: In digital media, a watermark is often a semi-transparent logo or text overlaid onto the content.

questions.stem: Which purpose of a watermark involves content creators asserting ownership and discouraging unauthorised use?
questions.explanation: Copyright protection: creators use watermarks to assert ownership, discourage unauthorised use and help identify the original creator.

questions.stem: Why might a company add its logo as a watermark to content shared online?
options: To prevent the content from being opened
For branding, promoting brand recognition even when the content is shared
questions.explanation: Watermarks serve branding purposes: companies add logos or brand names to promote brand recognition when content is shared online.

questions.stem: How can watermarks serve a security purpose for internal documents?
options: They discourage leaks or unauthorised distribution of confidential documents
They automatically delete the document after reading
They restrict who can log in to the document system
They compress the document for storage
questions.explanation: Companies add watermarks to internal documents to discourage leaks or unauthorised distribution of confidential material.

questions.stem: How are watermarks embedded in physical documents such as banknotes or certificates?
options: Printed on top after the document is finished
Stamped by hand at the point of issue
Attached as a separate hologram sticker
questions.explanation: For physical documents such as banknotes, watermarks are embedded during the papermaking process and serve as authentication.

questions.stem: What purpose do watermarks serve on banknotes and certificates?
options: Authentication, to verify the document's legitimacy
questions.explanation: On physical documents like banknotes, watermarks serve as a form of authentication to verify legitimacy.

questions.stem: In which contexts are watermarks said to be commonly used?
questions.explanation: Watermarks are commonly used in photography, art, documents and currency.

questions.stem: What caution is given about using watermarks?
options: They must always be placed in the top-left corner
They should never be used on digital content
They are legally required on all published images
They should be fully opaque to be effective
They should be used thoughtfully to avoid distracting from the main content, and not every situation requires one
questions.explanation: Watermarks should be applied thoughtfully to avoid distracting from the main content, and the purpose and context should be considered before using one.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a stated purpose of a watermark?
options: Encrypting the content so it cannot be read
questions.explanation: A watermark is a visual identification or protection method; it conveys information, asserts ownership or enhances security but does not encrypt content.
